SARS-CoVs encode two RNA cap MTases which sequentially methylate RNA cap at guanine N7 and RNA ribose 2-O positions, catalyze by nsp14 and nsp16, respectively.
we determined the biochemical properties and structural details of the SARS-CoV RNA 2′-o-methyltransferase (MTase) and its stimulatory factor, nsp10.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which SARS coronavirus RNA ribose 2'-O-methylation is catalyzed by the viral non-structural proteins nsp16 and nsp10.
the biochemical and structural characterization of the RNA 5′-capping enzyme from the SARS coronavirus, which is a key enzyme for viral replication.
the biochemical characterization and the structural analysis of the SARS coronavirus nsp16 MTases, which will provide important information to develop anti-coronavirus therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SARS coronavirus RNA 2′-o-methylation by nps16 requires nsp10, and nsp16/nps10 complex is the drug target for anti-coronavirus drug development.
nsp10 plays an essential role in SARS-CoV RNA cap modification, and nsp16 and nsp10 together form a functional MTase complex that is essential for SARS-CoVs to replicate and cause diseases in human.

the structure of the npsp16/nsp10 protein complex bound to SAM provides a basis for further understanding of the molecular mechanism of SARS-CoVs RNA cap formation and the potential for developing novel anti-coronavirus therapeutics.

the SARS-CoV cap MTase system consists of two independent MTases nsp14 and nsp16, which are both SAM-dependent and sequence-specific.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the structure of the SARS coronavirus 2′-methyltransferase complex reveals the molecular mechanism by which nsp10 activates nsp16 to catalyze RNA cap 2′-methylation, and provides a structural basis for the development of novel antiviral agents that target this enzyme complex.
nsp10, which is conserved among SARS-related coronaviruses, is a potential drug target for developing broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus agents.
